phase: Phase 7.3 — partial materialization / observation views: random-access query cost vs generic compressors on a 32.22 MiB, 800-object PDF
claim: On a 33,789,340 B (32.22 MiB) deterministic 800-stream PDF, the indexed partial-materialization lane (PDF_DEFLATE_REPLAY_RANS_INDEXED) serves all 18 pre-registered queries byte-exactly and reduces random-access DECODE WORK: at every query at >= ~2 MiB it touches ~0.41-0.46 MB (descriptor_bytes_traversed + entropy_bytes_decoded) regardless of offset, versus gzip inflating a+len (1.4%-2.3% of gzip's bytes in the late region), and is ~2-5x faster than gzip and ~4-13x faster than xz on CPU in the late region. It does NOT win in the early region (<= ~8 MiB), does NOT beat zstd's raw decompression speed at any point, has ~38 MB peak RSS versus gzip's ~1.2 MB, still loses whole-file size ~2.98x to xz (best VOLE 17,392,713 B vs xz 5,841,896 B), and — the decisive v1 caveat — reads and parses the WHOLE 17.5 MB descriptor, so on-disk I/O is NOT reduced (gzip reads a ~9.8 MB compressed prefix at 31 MiB). descriptor_bytes_traversed is a CPU-side approximation. Verdict: scoped positive on decode CPU/allocation; no I/O win yet; a seek/mmap reader is the prerequisite for any bytes-read claim.
command: dev: pdf-make-large 800; tools: qpdf --check + gs; dev: encode --force {pdf-deflate-replay-rans-indexed,byte-rans,pdf-physical}; baseline: gzip/zstd/xz/brotli compression; baseline: tools/baselines.sh; baseline: tools/partial-court.sh queries.jsonl ...; jq -rs -f tools/partial-table.jq
verdict: SCOPED POSITIVE (decode CPU/allocation); whole-file and on-disk-I/O claims remain losses
